title: FP8 activation heuristics: stability buckets, per-layer sanity checks, and regression gates for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable safe, production-grade FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) activation on Hopper GPUs by introducing stability buckets, per-layer sanity checks, and automatic regression gates. This ticket builds an adaptive activation heuristic that decides E4M3 vs E5M2 per-layer at rollout time and adds telemetry and automatic rollback triggers to avoid silent quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Activation heuristic selects E4M3/E5M2 per-layer with documented thresholds and deterministic fallback rules
No more than 5% of canary prompts show >1.5% absolute quality regression vs INT8 baseline after canary traffic (measured on the eval prompt set)
Telemetry emits activation decisions, per-layer sanity failures, and a regression score for each canary request
Automatic rollback triggers when regression score crosses configured thresholds for N consecutive minutes
Calibration harness can re-run synthetic calibration and produce updated profile artifacts and human-readable calibration reports
design_decisions: Use a two-stage decision: lightweight per-layer statistic check (mean/var of activation ranges) followed by a fast synthetic mini-calibration for ambiguous layers
Group layers into stability buckets (stable/high-confidence, borderline, volatile) and apply more conservative quant params for volatile bucket
Prefer E4M3 for layers with tight activation tails; prefer E5M2 in layers showing rounding noise sensitivity in synthetic calibration
Canary traffic split by token length and percentile of sequence types to surface KV-cache and attention-length related regressions
Expose a runtime flag to force global FP8 mode for debugging and support-runbook reproduction
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Scoped work and drafted calibration harness prototype (Marco). Linked initial prompt cohorts in Confluence.
2025-02-18: Implemented telemetry keys for per-layer activation stats and canary annotations. Deployed to staging runtime-1.22-alpha.
2025-02-24: Ran first synthetic calibration sweep across 10 models; discovered systematic tail clipping on attention output in layer groups 8-12 for transformer-large family.
2025-02-27: Adjusted heuristic thresholds; added a mini-calibration fallback for borderline layers. Observed improvement on validation set (AUC up by 0.9%).

2025-03-03: Canary rollout to 2% traffic with length-stratified sampling. Early telemetry shows 0.6% median regression vs INT8 baseline, one model exceeded the 1.5% threshold — triggered alert, paused canary for that model.

2025-03-05: Root cause investigation: stochastic rounding interaction with KV-cache reuse identified; plan to add cache-cohort tests and a short-term guard to force E5M2 for layers interacting with long-lived KV entries.
test_plan: Unit tests for activation statistics collectors and per-layer bucket assignment
Integration tests for synthetic mini-calibration that validate output ranges and deterministic reproducibility
Regression harness: run canary eval suite (multi-lingual prompts, few-shot, and long-context attention tests) comparing FP8 profile to INT8 baseline
Fault-injection tests where we toggle stochastic rounding noise to ensure guards catch regressions
Load test at 2% canary traffic for 72 hours with observability dashboards capturing regression score, token latency, and error rates
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): deploy heuristic and telemetry to runtime-1.22-alpha; run synthetic calibration on nightly batch
Phase 1 (canary): 2% production traffic length-stratified for 48-72h; automated checks run every 30m; human review at 24h
Phase 2 (ramp): 10% traffic if canary passes for 72h; continue rolling metric checks and expand prompt cohorts
Phase 3 (full): 100% traffic and create archived calibration-artifacts + release notes
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback trigger: regression_score > 1.5% absolute for 15m across 3 contiguous 5-minute windows
Manual rollback: on SRE/ML-owner approval if telemetry shows rising error-rate or latency > SLA
Fallback policy: if rollback occurs, revert to INT8 profile and re-run synthetic calibration with relaxed thresholds, then schedule a remediation patch
Post-mortem: within 48h of rollback, produce incident report with telemetry slices and suggested fix
notes: Trade-off: running mini-calibration on borderline layers increases per-request CPU overhead during calibration windows but dramatically reduces silent regressions.
We observed per-language drift (notably JP and ES cohorts) — will consider language-aware thresholds in follow-up ticket.
Ops: add a 'fp8.activation.force_mode' runtime flag to aid debugging and customer support reproductions.
Follow-up: schedule a cross-team review with SRE to tune automatic rollback thresholds and alerting playbook (target: Cycle 43).
